newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate higher on liquidity demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate higher on liquidity demand.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates edged up 15 basis points to 17.45 percent in early trade on Friday on what dealers put down to light liquidty pressure due to demand for cash ahead of the weekend.
"Rates often come under pressure ahead of the weekend," a dealer said.
Dealers said they did not foresee a heavy liquidity shortage and thus did not expect rates to increase much further.
"There is a fair amount of liquidity, and that together with mild inflation figures released yesterday should keep rates in check," another trader said.
Banco de Mexico announced on Thursday as trade was closing in the money market, that consumer prices rose by 0.48 percent during the first half of July.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile declined 80 basis points to 18.30 percent.
Liquidity of just 1 million pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations.
